title: Brake Force Imbalance - System Configuration
shortDescription: Brake force imbalance system configuration mismatch.
fullDescription: The ABS/EBD module has detected that the brake force distribution configuration does not match the vehicle build data. This often follows a control module replacement or BCM recalibration where the variant coding for axle, tire size, or drive layout was not entered correctly.
safetyImpact: Uneven braking can pull the vehicle to one side under hard stops, increasing crash risk.

causes.cause: Worn or contaminated brake pads on one corner
Faulty wheel speed or pressure sensor

symptoms: Vehicle pulls to one side when braking

fixSteps.title: Scan All Modules
fixSteps.instruction: Connect a bidirectional scan tool and read live data for wheel speeds, brake pressure, and yaw rate. Note which corner deviates from the others.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Pads and Calipers
fixSteps.instruction: Lift the vehicle and inspect each caliper for free movement of slide pins and even pad wear. Replace any pad set worn unevenly or any seized caliper.

fixSteps.title: Check Hydraulic System
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect brake hoses for swelling or internal collapse. Pressure-test the master cylinder if pressure correlation faults are present.

fixSteps.title: Calibrate or Replace HCU
fixSteps.instruction: Recalibrate yaw and steering angle sensors after repair. Replace the HCU only if internal valve leakage is confirmed by pressure decay testing.

faq.q: Is it safe to drive with a brake force imbalance code?
faq.a: No. Stopping distances may increase and the vehicle may pull during braking. Have it repaired before further driving.

faq.q: Will new pads fix this code?
faq.a: Often yes when the pads are unevenly worn, but a sticking caliper or hose must be addressed first or the new pads will wear unevenly again.

title: EPS Steering Torque Input Signal
shortDescription: Steering torque input signal out of expected range.
fullDescription: The electric power steering control module has determined that the torque sensor input signal is outside the calibrated range for the current steering angle and vehicle speed. The PCM also receives this data over CAN to coordinate stability events.
safetyImpact: Loss or reduction of power steering assist sharply increases effort needed at parking speeds and during evasive maneuvers.

causes.cause: Failed EPS torque or steering angle sensor
Low battery voltage or weak charging system

symptoms: EPS or steering warning lamp on
Audible whine or click from column

fixSteps.title: Verify Battery and Charging
fixSteps.instruction: Measure battery voltage at rest and under load. Confirm alternator output between 13.8 and 14.6 V. EPS faults often follow weak batteries.

fixSteps.title: Read EPS Module Data
fixSteps.instruction: Use a capable scan tool to read EPS module data including torque sensor, motor current, and supply voltage. Note any CAN timeout DTCs.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wiring and Grounds
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the EPS power feed, ground stud, and CAN harness at the column. Look for chafed insulation near the steering shaft.

fixSteps.title: Calibrate or Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Perform steering angle and torque sensor calibration. Replace the column or module if internal faults persist after wiring is verified.

faq.q: Can I drive with reduced EPS assist?
faq.a: Short distances at low speed are possible, but parking and emergency maneuvers will be much harder. Repair promptly.

faq.q: Does the EPS module need programming after replacement?
faq.a: Yes. Most EPS modules require coding to the VIN and a steering angle calibration before assist is restored.

title: Steering Angle Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: Steering angle sensor (SAS) circuit malfunction.
fullDescription: The stability control module has detected an electrical fault in the steering angle sensor circuit, either an open, short, or implausible signal change versus yaw rate.
safetyImpact: Loss of steering angle data disables stability control and may reduce EPS assist, affecting handling in emergencies.

causes.cause: Faulty steering angle or torque sensor
Sensor calibration not performed after service
EPS or ABS module 5V reference fault

fixSteps.title: Read Live Sensor Data
fixSteps.instruction: View steering angle and torque sensor live data while turning the wheel lock-to-lock. Confirm smooth, monotonic output.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Clockspring
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the lower steering column trim and inspect the clockspring connector and ribbon for damage.

fixSteps.title: Calibrate Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: With the wheels straight, perform the zero-point reset procedure with a scan tool. Recheck for fault recurrence.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor or Column
fixSteps.instruction: If the sensor fails to learn or readings remain implausible, replace the SAS or column assembly per service information.

faq.q: Why did this code set after an alignment?
faq.a: Alignment changes the steering wheel zero position. The SAS must be relearned with a scan tool afterward.

faq.q: Can I clear this without a scan tool?
faq.a: No, most vehicles require a bidirectional command to relearn the steering angle zero point.

title: Steering Torque Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: Steering torque sensor circuit malfunction.
fullDescription: The EPS torque sensor, typically a dual-coil magnetic device, is reporting two channels that disagree or one channel that has gone open/short. Assist is disabled when this fault sets.
safetyImpact: Loss of steering angle data disables stability control and may reduce EPS assist, affecting handling in emergencies.

causes.cause: Faulty steering angle or torque sensor
Sensor calibration not performed after service
EPS or ABS module 5V reference fault

fixSteps.title: Read Live Sensor Data
fixSteps.instruction: View steering angle and torque sensor live data while turning the wheel lock-to-lock. Confirm smooth, monotonic output.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Clockspring
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the lower steering column trim and inspect the clockspring connector and ribbon for damage.

fixSteps.title: Calibrate Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: With the wheels straight, perform the zero-point reset procedure with a scan tool. Recheck for fault recurrence.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor or Column
fixSteps.instruction: If the sensor fails to learn or readings remain implausible, replace the SAS or column assembly per service information.

faq.q: Why did this code set after an alignment?
faq.a: Alignment changes the steering wheel zero position. The SAS must be relearned with a scan tool afterward.

faq.q: Can I clear this without a scan tool?
faq.a: No, most vehicles require a bidirectional command to relearn the steering angle zero point.

title: Steering Sensor Power Supply
shortDescription: Steering sensor 5V reference supply out of range.
fullDescription: The 5V reference shared by the steering angle and torque sensors is outside specification. Causes include a shorted sensor pulling the supply down or a failed regulator inside the EPS module.
safetyImpact: Loss of steering angle data disables stability control and may reduce EPS assist, affecting handling in emergencies.

title: EPS Column Motor Circuit Open
shortDescription: EPS column motor circuit open.
fullDescription: The EPS module has detected no current flow through the column motor when assist was commanded. The fault is typically a broken motor lead, internal brush failure, or a stuck-open motor relay.
safetyImpact: Loss of column-mounted EPS assist sharply increases steering effort and may indicate a mechanical bind that worsens handling.

causes.cause: EPS motor brush or winding failure
Mechanical bind in column or U-joint

symptoms: Battery drain after key-off in some cases

fixSteps.title: Verify Mechanical Movement
fixSteps.instruction: With ignition off, turn the wheel slowly lock to lock by hand and feel for binding or grinding before electrical testing.

fixSteps.title: Test Motor Circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the column motor connector and measure resistance across phases. Compare to specification; expect a few tenths of an ohm and balanced phases.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Resolver Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the small-signal connector for the position sensor. Backprobe and check for shielded pair continuity to the EPS module.

fixSteps.title: Replace Column Assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Most column EPS units are serviced as an assembly. Replace and perform the required programming and steering angle relearn.

faq.q: Can the EPS motor be repaired separately?
faq.a: On most platforms the column is sold as a unit and the motor is not separately serviced.

faq.q: Will a steering angle relearn fix this?
faq.a: No. These are hardware faults; calibration is only the final step after repair.

title: Hydraulic Boost Pressure Sensor
shortDescription: Hydraulic boost system pressure sensor circuit fault.
fullDescription: The hydraulic-assisted brake or steering boost system reports a pressure sensor signal that is out of plausible range. Common on hybrid vehicles where an electric pump pressurizes the booster reservoir.
safetyImpact: Loss of hydraulic boost can lengthen brake pedal travel and require much higher pedal effort, increasing stopping distance.

fixSteps.title: Check Fluid and Leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the booster reservoir for correct level and the surrounding plumbing for leaks. Top up only with the specified fluid.

fixSteps.title: Observe Pump Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Use a scan tool to view accumulator pressure and pump run time during pressure build. Excessive run time indicates a leak or worn pump.

fixSteps.title: Test Accumulator
fixSteps.instruction: Pressurize the system, key-off, then count brake pedal applications until pressure dumps. Fewer than spec indicates a failed accumulator.

fixSteps.title: Replace Components
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the pump or accumulator as indicated, bleed the system per manufacturer procedure, and clear codes. Hybrid systems require special bleed routines.

faq.q: Is this safe to drive?
faq.a: Often no. Without boost, brake effort is several times normal. Tow if pedal is hard.

faq.q: Can I bleed this like a normal system?
faq.a: No. Hybrid hydraulic boosters require a scan tool to cycle valves during the bleed.
